## Sound and music

Check ctx.audio or use requireAudio. The host owns Audio, decoded WAV effects
and encoded music sources until teardown; games retain SoundHandle/MusicHandle
values only. Handles belong to that Audio service; there is no individual
unload. AssetCollection.deinit does not release them.

These actual portable helpers load once and play on an event. Optional
audio is output: the game stays playable when a browser lacks a user gesture
or the device is unavailable. Catch errors where that policy is appropriate;
other games may report them to the player.

[Compiled source](../../examples/asset_recipes.zig#L18) (`loadEffect`):

```zig
pub fn loadEffect(ctx: *up.core.GameContext) ?up.core.Audio.SoundHandle {
    const audio = ctx.audio orelse return null;
    return audio.loadWav(@embedFile("assets/blip.wav")) catch null;
}
```

[Compiled source](../../examples/asset_recipes.zig#L24) (`playEffect`):

```zig
pub fn playEffect(ctx: *up.core.GameContext, effect: ?up.core.Audio.SoundHandle) void {
    const audio = ctx.audio orelse return;
    _ = audio.play(effect orelse return, .{ .volume = 0.25 }) catch {};
}
```


play can return `AudioUnavailable`; malformed WAV/music input and invalid
handles/options remain errors. The presence of a host service does not imply
ready output. Do not call Audio.deinit on a borrowed context service.

For music, load once and retain the returned optional handle in Game, then
play on an appropriate event. A blocked browser play can be retried with the
same handle after a gesture; do not reload the track on every retry.

[Compiled source](../../examples/api_reference_recipes.zig#L64) (`loadMusic`):

```zig
pub fn loadMusic(ctx: *up.core.GameContext) !?up.core.Audio.MusicHandle {
    const audio = ctx.audio orelse return null;
    return try audio.loadMusic(@embedFile("assets/tone.ogg"), .{});
}
```

[Compiled source](../../examples/api_reference_recipes.zig#L69) (`playMusic`):

```zig
pub fn playMusic(ctx: *up.core.GameContext, handle: ?up.core.Audio.MusicHandle) void {
    const audio = ctx.audio orelse return;
    _ = audio.playMusic(handle orelse return, .{ .loop = true, .volume = 0.5 }) catch {};
}
```


These helpers run against a logical Audio host natively and in Wasm, including
incremental OGG decode to nonzero PCM and a blocked retry. This checks the
recipe, not physical speaker output. Format defaults to OGG/Vorbis; WAV requires
`.format = .wav`.
One incremental music stream is active; starting another replaces it after
successful start. SFX can overlap. pauseMusic/resumeMusic/stopMusic return
whether a playback was controlled. Defaults and types are below; the
[audio guide](../guides/audio-assets.md) and
[Neon Siege](../../dogfood/neon-siege/src/game.zig) show full music setup.
Logical requests, not device scheduling or speaker samples, are replayed.

<a id="core-Audio"></a>
## `up.core.Audio`

[Source declaration](../../src/audio.zig#L378).

A small, host-owned sound-effect service for `GameProtocol` games.

`loadWav` decodes bytes once and returns a reusable handle. The service owns
every decoded sound and releases it in `deinit`, after stopping its mixer.
A game therefore stores handles but never frees individual sound resources.
This intentionally covers short WAV effects; the lower-level `AudioMixer`
and `AssetStore` APIs remain available for advanced/native use cases.

[Source declaration](../../src/audio.zig#L411).

OGG/Vorbis is the default because it is the compact, incrementally
decoded long-form path on every supported host. WAV is accepted for

<a id="core-Audio-MusicDiagnostics"></a>
### `up.core.Audio.MusicDiagnostics`

[Source declaration](../../src/audio.zig#L439).

A small observation surface shared by native developer diagnostics.
`underruns` is currently always zero: music decode/refill happens
synchronously before host PCM submission rather than in an audio
callback. It is retained as an explicit statement of that behavior,
not a device-underrun measurement.

Fields, variants and defaults (methods follow):

```zig
struct {
    state: MusicState = .stopped,
    encoded_bytes: usize = 0,
    source_frames: usize = 0,
    decoder_position_frames: usize = 0,
    buffered_frames: usize = 0,
    buffer_capacity_frames: usize = 0,
    underruns: u32 = 0,
}
```

<a id="core-Audio-PlayOptions"></a>
### `up.core.Audio.PlayOptions`

[Source declaration](../../src/audio.zig#L451).

Per-request controls. Volume is finite and in the inclusive range
`0.0...1.0`; looping repeats the decoded effect until stopped.

Fields, variants and defaults (methods follow):

<a id="core-Audio-loadWav"></a>
### `up.core.Audio.loadWav`

[Source declaration](../../src/audio.zig#L511).

Decodes a small WAV effect from game-owned bytes. This performs no I/O;
`@embedFile` is the portable way to load a starter-sized effect during
`Game.init` on both desktop and browser builds.

```zig
pub fn loadWav(self: *Audio, bytes: []const u8) !SoundHandle;
```

<a id="core-Audio-loadMusic"></a>
### `up.core.Audio.loadMusic`

[Source declaration](../../src/audio.zig#L526).

Retains encoded game-owned bytes and creates a source suitable for
bounded, incremental playback. No full-track PCM allocation occurs.
OGG/Vorbis is the default; select `.wav` explicitly for WAV source.

```zig
pub fn loadMusic(self: *Audio, bytes: []const u8, options: MusicLoadOptions) !MusicHandle;
```

<a id="core-Audio-play"></a>
### `up.core.Audio.play`

[Source declaration](../../src/audio.zig#L544).

Starts an independent playback instance. It is safe to play the same
loaded effect concurrently. A blocked or unavailable host returns a
recoverable error and does not create a hidden queued playback.

```zig
pub fn play(self: *Audio, sound: SoundHandle, options: PlayOptions) !PlaybackHandle;
```

<a id="core-Audio-playMusic"></a>
### `up.core.Audio.playMusic`

[Source declaration](../../src/audio.zig#L554).

Starts the selected music source. At most one high-level music stream
is active; a successful new request stops the previous music stream.
Sound effects continue to mix independently on the SFX bus.

```zig
pub fn playMusic(self: *Audio, music: MusicHandle, options: MusicPlayOptions) !PlaybackHandle;
```

The Audio methods' source-local PlaybackHandle is `up.assets.PlaybackHandle`.
It identifies a playback instance rather than its loaded sound/music source.
Audio's nested options and handles use the `up.core.Audio.*` path.

## Progress bytes

SaveStore is a borrowed host capability. Keys are identifiers, not paths:
1–64 ASCII letters/numbers/dot/underscore/hyphen, with no consecutive dots.
The game chooses serialization, versioning and migration. Built-in hosts
namespace saves; there is no portable general filesystem API.

These functions encode four explicit little-endian bytes. Missing,
unavailable, malformed or rejected storage falls back to score zero or a
recoverable write failure; no raw struct memory is persisted.

[Compiled source](../../examples/asset_recipes.zig#L29) (`loadProgress`):

```zig
pub fn loadProgress(ctx: *up.core.GameContext) u32 {
    const saves = ctx.save_data orelse return 0;
    var bytes: [4]u8 = undefined;
    const stored = saves.read("recipe-progress", &bytes) catch return 0;
    if (stored.len != bytes.len) return 0;
    return std.mem.readInt(u32, &bytes, .little);
}
```

[Compiled source](../../examples/asset_recipes.zig#L37) (`saveProgress`):

```zig
pub fn saveProgress(ctx: *up.core.GameContext, score: u32) void {
    const saves = ctx.save_data orelse return;
    var bytes: [4]u8 = undefined;
    std.mem.writeInt(u32, &bytes, score, .little);
    saves.write("recipe-progress", &bytes) catch {};
}
```


read returns a slice borrowing your destination. readAlloc returns an owned
buffer which you must free with the supplied allocator; max_bytes bounds
both allocation and accepted blob size. `NotFound` is different from an
existing empty value; `TooLarge` can mean the destination is too small.
Built-in writes replace a whole key on success and preserve its previous value
on failure. This is not a multi-key transaction or a power-loss durability
guarantee. Error is enumerated below. Native paths, browser localStorage and
host limits are in [save data](../guides/save-data.md).

<a id="core-SaveStore"></a>
## `up.core.SaveStore`

[Source declaration](../../src/save_data.zig#L9).

Backend-neutral persistence for small, game-owned byte blobs.

A store is supplied by the host through `GameContext.save_data`. Keys are
portable identifiers, not paths: they are limited to ASCII letters,
numbers, `.`, `_`, and `-`. The game owns the bytes' format and any
versioning or migration policy.

<a id="core-SaveStore-readAlloc"></a>
### `up.core.SaveStore.readAlloc`

[Source declaration](../../src/save_data.zig#L55).

Allocates and returns the full stored blob. The caller owns the result
and must free it with the same allocator. `max_bytes` bounds both the
allocation and the accepted stored size.

```zig
pub fn readAlloc(self: *const SaveStore, allocator: std.mem.Allocator, key: []const u8, max_bytes: usize) Error![]u8;
```

<a id="core-SaveStore-write"></a>
### `up.core.SaveStore.write`

[Source declaration](../../src/save_data.zig#L70).

Replaces one blob. Built-in stores publish the complete value only on
success; a failed write preserves the previous value and other keys.
This is per-key replacement, not a multi-key transaction or a promise
of durability after power loss. Custom hosts must uphold this contract.

```zig
pub fn write(self: *const SaveStore, key: []const u8, bytes: []const u8) Error!void;
```

<a id="core-SaveStore-isValidApplicationId"></a>
### `up.core.SaveStore.isValidApplicationId`

[Source declaration](../../src/save_data.zig#L96).

Browser callback games declare `pub const storage_id = "...";` so the
browser host can keep their localStorage keys separate. Desktop games
use `sdl.Config.organization` plus `sdl.Config.application` instead.

```zig
pub fn isValidApplicationId(application_id: []const u8) bool;
```
